**Team Asobi** is a Japanese [video game developer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_developer "Video game developer") based in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"). A [first-party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-party_developer "First-party developer") studio for [Sony Interactive Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Interactive_Entertainment "Sony Interactive Entertainment"), Team Asobi was originally formed in 2012 as part of [Japan Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_Studio "Japan Studio"), but formally spun off into an independent studio within Sony's [PlayStation Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Studios "PlayStation Studios") in April 2021. It is best known for the _[Astro Bot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro_Bot_\(series\) "Astro Bot \(series\)")_ series.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-As_PS_Studio_3-2)
## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Asobi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Team_Asobi_logo_%282018%E2%80%932021%29.png/250px-Team_Asobi_logo_%282018%E2%80%932021%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Team_Asobi_logo_\(2018%E2%80%932021\).png)First logo (2018–2021)
Team Asobi was first formed in 2012 as an internal part of [Japan Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_Studio "Japan Studio") based in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo") by Nicolas Doucet.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-As_PS_Studio_1-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-Small_overview-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-5) The team's name is derived from the Japanese word "Asobi",[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-6) meaning "Play".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-As_PS_Studio_1-3) After forming, they worked on technical demos and went on to develop _[The Playroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Playroom_\(2013_video_game\) "The Playroom \(2013 video game\)")_ (2013), a pre-downloaded augmented reality game designed to demonstrate the use of the [PlayStation Camera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Camera "PlayStation Camera") and [DualShock 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DualShock_4 "DualShock 4") for the [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-Small_overview-4) Doucet and several members of his team had been developers for games for the [EyeToy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EyeToy "EyeToy") and had brought their knowledge forward for use on _The Playroom_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-Playroom_info_2013-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-psblog_playroom_vr-8) Team Asobi also created a virtual reality version _The Playroom VR_ to demonstrate the [PlayStation VR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_VR "PlayStation VR") unit with its release in 2016.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-psblog_playroom_vr-8) _The Playroom_ introduced a small robotic character, then named "A5081" which visually resembles the word "ASOBI",[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-9) and became the reference for the Astro Bot character used in their later games, _[Astro Bot Rescue Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro_Bot_Rescue_Mission "Astro Bot Rescue Mission")_ (2018), _[Astro's Playroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro's_Playroom "Astro's Playroom")_ (2020), and the winner of [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Game_of_the_Year_awards "List of Game of the Year awards") at [The Game Awards 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024 "The Game Awards 2024") and the [28th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/28th_Annual_D.I.C.E._Awards "28th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards"), _[Astro Bot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro_Bot "Astro Bot")_ (2024).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-As_PS_Studio_1-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-10)
Across late 2020 and early 2021, several staff members of Japan Studio, outside those of Team Asobi, announced their departure; Sony later affirmed that by April 2021, Japan Studio would be refocused around Team Asobi based on the success of _Astro's Playroom_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-11) In June 2021, Sony announced that Team Asobi had been transitioned to a standalone studio within [PlayStation Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Studios "PlayStation Studios").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-As_PS_Studio_1-3)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-As_PS_Studio_2-12)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-As_PS_Studio_3-2) Doucet remains Asobi's studio director and creative director following this transition.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-As_PS_Studio_3-2) Since January 6, 2025, _Astro Bot_ has become the most awarded platformer game of all time, beating out _[It Takes Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It_Takes_Two_\(video_game\) "It Takes Two \(video game\)")_ with a current total of 106 Game of the Year nominations and wins.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Asobi#cite_note-GR-13)
